1. The Global Problem & Macro Inefficiencies

  • The Global Logistics Bottleneck: Total global logistics spending commands between $11 Trillion and $13 Trillion annually , crippled by fragmented infrastructure and structural delays.
  • The $800 Billion Administrative Drain: Cross-border friction, manual customs compliance, and port demurrage waste up to $800 Billion in economic value each year.
  • Physical Sourcing Vulnerabilities: Industrial supply chains face severe cyber threats on legacy Operational Technology (OT), combined with a global shortage of qualified cyber-physical engineering talent.
  • Digital Commerce Vulnerabilities: Global B2B and retail e-commerce networks lose massive volumes to counterfeit goods, phantom inventory, and upfront capital exposure without independent quality validation.

↑ Index

2. The Integrated Solution: Four Initiatives, One Ledger

Delper Integrated merges four initiatives into a single economic engine, operating exclusively via the 100% fiat-backed ERC-20 Delper Token:

  • Project Iron Nexus ($46.00 Trillion): A global multimodal transport grid linking deepwater ports, dedicated electrified rail corridors, express highways, and high-velocity air cargo hubs. Rail freight is designed to cut transport energy use by 60%.
  • Project Make in India 🇮🇳 ($56.00 Trillion): A coastal software-defined manufacturing matrix in India. Approximately 560,000 dark factories on 1-acre coastal footprints are powered by 840 GW of dedicated zero-carbon nuclear baseload. Across a 7,500 km coastal corridor, these factories are projected to capture 28% of the world's physical manufacturing value-add. At 2024 world levels this is an after-tax profit of about $4.71 trillion per year, which is repaid to bondholders from the pooled net profit. Bharat starts after Iron Nexus is operative in Year 15: its profit begins in Year 19 and reaches full scale in Year 27.
  • Delper Aegis ($247.7 Billion ARR): An enterprise-tier industrial cybersecurity layer. Each production line sits behind an inline Delper Guard firewall targeting IEC 62443 Security Level 4 (SL-4), with a physical write-lock that blocks remote programming exploits.
  • Delper Global Trust Infrastructure: A buyer-first verified sourcing platform. Track A (Bulk) carries a 15.184% fixed transaction rate, and Track B (Retail) carries 24.2%. Both run on a 14-day settlement cycle.

Human Capital & Cyber-Physical Defence

  • 560,000 Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) per year: Each dark factory hub runs 7 FDEs for 24/7/365 monitoring across three 8-hour shifts. Training runs through a 12-month, online, credit-bearing Post-Graduate Advanced Diploma in Forward Deployed Engineering and Cyber-Physical Security, delivered via UVCE, Bangalore University, and scales to 2,147 physical hubs by Year 3.
  • Coastal Defence Umbrella: The Indian Navy enforces a Maritime Domain Awareness bubble. Mid-tier lanes are covered by BrahMos batteries, and perimeters are protected by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) with anti-drone interceptor domes and air-gapped private 5G cores.

4. Immediate Capital Ask & Strategic Use of Funds

The USD 8.00 Million investor cash is restated to match the costed build plan. Items marked "to be priced" are held until quotes are received, and the reserve is released only on Group approval. This restated split replaces the earlier Track A and Track B allocation, and it needs the investor's agreement before it is final.

Costed build, internal team: $0.987M

  • Track A build [$0.485M]: architecture and control design, policy rules, data residency and consent, enforcement layer, observability, security baseline.
  • Track B build [$0.502M]: agent build, channel connectors, kill switch and finance-lock tests, independent control review, soft launch in UAE and Singapore.

External items, to be priced: $2.915M

  • SAP and systems [$0.915M]: SAP BTP and Signavio process mapping, SAP S/4HANA core ERP, and SGS quality-control webhooks, previously in Track A core systems and business process capital.
  • 3PQC infrastructure [$0.80M]: partner onboarding, structural audits and independent quality assurance.
  • Escrow, legal and licensing [$0.50M]: bank partner compliance, cross-border contracts and regulatory clearances.
  • Supplier RTB vetting [$0.40M]: factory onboarding and vendor verification.
  • Cloud and integration [$0.30M]: Shopify, WooCommerce and ONDC buyer endpoint connectors.

Operational contingency: $0.40M

Capital cushion against transaction latency in early processing loops.

Pre-shipment escrow margin: $2.60M (recycled, not spent)

A revolving liquidity margin on consecutive FOB payments. It is working capital, not a cost, and it is returned as payments recycle.

Reserve, held pending Group approval: $1.098M

Covers team capacity not yet costed in the build plan. It is released only on Group approval, once the build plan is extended or quotes are received.

Check: $0.987M + $2.915M + $0.40M + $2.60M + $1.098M = $8.00M.

5. Investor Risk Mitigation: The 12-Month Exit Pipe

The USD 8.00 Million investor commitment is insulated by a parallel commodity monetization facility that operates independently of the core technology tracks.

The isolated financial vehicle for GK Bharta

  • Route: 1,000,000 metric tons of bulk palm oil annually, via irrevocable at-sight letters of credit (LCs).
  • Revenue: GK Bharta earns USD 15.00 Million of post-tax palm oil revenue within the first 12 months.

Seed repayment and equity transfer

Palm oil revenue from GK Bharta funds the Year 1 retirement of the USD 8.00 Million investor loan, including 11% interest, totaling USD 8.88 Million, and the USD 4.00 Million Radiant Synage payment. The investor's 40% and Radiant Synage's 60% stakes are sold to GK Bharta at Month 12, so GK Bharta is the 100% owner from Year 2. Net cash risk to the investor drops to USD 0.00 at Month 12. Cash distributions to GK Bharta begin only after all loans are cleared, in Year 36 on the base case.

6. Primary Unit Economics & Revenue Engines

Track A: Bulk Enterprise Trade

  • Fixed Transaction Rate: Captures a mandatory 15.184% fee on total Gross Merchandise Value (GMV).
  • High-Velocity Turnover: Achieves 26 capital turns per year via a 14-day settlement cycle from Year 2 onward (17.6 turns in Year 1).
  • Liquidity Spread: Generates a 6.0% net annual spread on asset-secured capital facilities using bonded cargo as collateral.

Track B: Verified Digital Marketplace

  • E-Commerce Take Rate: Captures 24.2% gross profit per order ($72.67 on a standard $300 customer checkout).
  • Real-Time Bidding (RTB) Model: Buyers search free; pre-vetted factories prepay RTB and physical Third-Party Quality Control (3PQC) costs at actual cost, preventing platform overhead.
  • Deducted Commissions: Platform commission and lead generation costs are deducted directly from vendor escrow balances only upon consumer satisfaction sign-off. Note that this is distinct from the 2% Transact Tax in Section 7, which is a protocol-level tax on token mint and burn.

Track 1 and Track 2 cash builds Aegis in Years 1 to 3. From Year 11, Track 1, Track 2 and Aegis revenue services and repays the loan as quickly as possible, and Iron Nexus income begins in Year 15. GK Bharta receives no profit share until all loans are cleared; from then on it receives 100% of net profit.

Delper Aegis: Factory-as-a-Service (FaaS)

  • Platform ARR: Delper Aegis carries a base ARR of $247.7 Billion at full scale, deployed through 1,963,334 Delper Guard inline hardware units across SME and enterprise tiers.
  • Tiered Hardware Margins: Targets 68% gross margin on SME chips and 82.3% gross margin on advanced 5nm dark factory chips.
  • Insulated Staffing Markup: Pass-through engineer costs are absorbed by the factory customer, while Delper retains a 20% clean profit markup on all field operations.

7. Macro Financing: Project Iron Nexus & Make in India 🇮🇳

The $102.00 Trillion programme is financed through the Delper Token economy, a supranational debt wrapper, and a fixed set of annual inflows:

The AAA Supranational Credit Enhancement Wrapper

  • The Deflationary Mechanism: Standard emerging-market debt pricing at 9.00% would compound construction liabilities far beyond the blueprint's launch balance.
  • Supranational Joint Guarantees: The World Bank Group (IBRD) and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) co-back an unconditional AAA guarantee over the construction tranches.
  • Yield Compression: The model keeps the 9.00% rate on both bond series, so the wrapper compression to 4.75%–5.50% is not applied. Final launch debt at Year 15 is $43.12 Trillion , after Years 1 to 14 repayments from bulk (Track 1) and retail (Track 2), including capitalized construction interest, refinanced as a 10-year bond.

The Macro Toll Engine

Once fully operational in Year 15, the network collects an optimized $3.98 Trillion gross annual toll . After a $270.27 Billion annual O&M budget , this delivers $3.71 Trillion in net operational toll cash flow :

  • Maritime Channels (35%): $1.39 Trillion per annum via automated TEU handling and deepwater berth access.
  • Rail & Highway Tariffs (32%): $1.28 Trillion per annum ($0.15/km truck tariffs; $0.02/cargo-ton-km rail tariffs).
  • Digital AI Customs Platforms (18%): $0.72 Trillion per annum generated from automated declaration processing fees.
  • Inland Warehousing & Air Hubs (15%): $0.59 Trillion per annum via climate-controlled staging and smart sorting.

8. Debt Retirement Schedule

Revised funding sequence (management direction)

Years 1 to 3: Track 1 and Track 2 revenue builds Aegis. Iron Nexus is built with 10-year bonds. From Year 11, Track 1, Track 2 and Aegis revenue services and clears the bonds as quickly as possible. Once Iron Nexus is operating, Bharat bonds are issued, and the loan is cleared with interest from the income of Track 1, Track 2, Aegis and Iron Nexus. Once all loans are cleared, 100% of profit goes to the GK Bharta account.

Rebuilt in Section 9 on this sequence. Iron Nexus income from Year 15 and the $52.59 trillion Iron Nexus bond balance are confirmed. Iron Nexus is retired in Year 27. Bharat is issued at the end of Year 27 and is cleared in Year 36. The Aegis launch cost of $1.82 billion is covered from Track 1 and Track 2 cash in Year 1.

At Year 15, construction tranches consolidate into two bond series, both carrying 9% per annum interest and issued as 10-year bonds. Bharat bonds are $56.00 Trillion. Iron Nexus bonds start at $52.59 Trillion ($46.00 Trillion principal plus $6.59 Trillion of capitalised construction interest). Repayments in Years 1 to 14 from bulk (Track 1) and retail (Track 2) reduce this to $43.12 Trillion.

Iron Nexus is bought back with 40% of Year 15 group inflow, and bulk (Track 1) and retail (Track 2) repayments reduce it from Year 15 on. From Year 16, the pool pays interest on Iron Nexus and then Iron Nexus principal. Bharat interest is capitalised into the Bharat balance while Iron Nexus is outstanding. Once Iron Nexus is cleared, Bharat interest and principal are paid from the pool. Nothing is distributed to GK Bharta until both series are retired.

Basis and assumptions

  • Group inflow: Years 1 to 10 ($0.300T) and Years 11 to 14 ($0.660T) are group period totals, spread evenly. From Year 15 it is the named streams of $5.24T a year.
  • Bharat profit: starts in Year 25, six years later than the original timing, at $0.42T in Years 25 to 28, $2.52T in Years 29 to 32 and $4.71T from Year 33.
  • Track 1: 15.184% × 70% × $3.6T trade, which is $0.383T a year, transferred to the pool from Year 7.
  • Track 2: retail repayment of $0.362T a year from Year 7.
  • Aegis build: Track 1 and Track 2 cash in Years 1 to 3 first covers the $1.82B launch cost.
  • Retained reserve of $0.03T a year in Years 1 to 10. From Year 11 no cash is retained.
  • O&M of $0.270T a year from Year 16.
  • Iron Nexus: the $52.59T construction balance ($46.00T principal plus $6.59T capitalised interest) is repaid from the pool in Years 1 to 14, leaving $39.41T at Year 15. From Year 15 it accrues 9% and is repaid first. Iron Nexus is cleared in Year 27.
  • Bharat: $56.00T is issued at the end of Year 27, after Iron Nexus is cleared. It accrues 9% from Year 28, and it is cleared in Year 36.
  • Distributions to GK Bharta start only after both series are cleared, so in Year 36. Palm oil revenue of $15.00M a year is GK Bharta income outside the pool, shown in Section 5.
  • Model check: total inflow of 640.32T equals debt repaid (160.14T), O&M (17.55T), retained reserve (0.30T) and distribution (462.33T).

10. Strategic Investment Summary, Validation Gates & Milestones

  • Blueprint Verdict: The Delper Integrated Master Blueprint states the programme is unconditionally viable, citing the token economy's 2% transaction tax, the $12.11 Trillion treasury float, and 24/7 software-defined manufacturing as drivers of rapid capital amortization.
  • Post-Debt Treasury: Once debt is retired, the project operates at macro profit margins, leaving the corporate entity an unencumbered treasury to capitalize future global trade expansion.
  • Immediate Milestone Gating: The multi-trillion-dollar expansion is insulated behind short-term operational proof gates: 
[Month 0-2: Framework Validation]  ──> Secure letters of intent from Axis Bank, ONDC, and SGS.

[Month 2-9: Cost-Per-Order Pilot]  ──> Run 300-500 transactions to verify supplier fee acceptance.

[Year 2-5: Network Scalability]    ──> Scale to 15,000 sellers before advancing Aegis FaaS capital.

Non-Negotiable Validation Gates (First 36 Months)

  1. Industrial Frame Stress Testing: Inject over 5,000,000 malformed frames per hour into 5nm FinFET Delper Guard processors to confirm self-quarantine without dropping robotic synchronization.
  2. 60-Day Shadow Mode: Passively record the first 4,000 Year 1 factory hulls for at least 60 days to build baseline models of Modbus/PROFINET traffic before live enforcement.
  3. Wafer Procurement Lock-In: Secure multi-year advanced node fabrication agreements with global foundries against semiconductor supply shocks.
  4. Legal Restructuring of Training Bonds: Complete a multi-jurisdictional review of student repayment terms so that ₹20.0 crore per-hub refund exposure is legally isolated from tuition revenue.
  5. Group Software Human Override Policy: All Delper software that makes or executes decisions affecting customers, traders, workers, public infrastructure, or safety must have a designed and tested human override before go-live. Each override needs a named owner, defined thresholds for when it applies, and an audit log of every use. Agentic systems, including customs clearance, must define in writing the actions they may take without approval and the actions reserved for a named human, such as customs holds, rejections, duty assessments, enforcement, and safety-related operations. An emergency halt must be tested, with a documented manual fallback. The 60-day shadow mode must measure override frequency and response time as well as detection accuracy.

11. ESG and SDG Alignment

This section maps the programme to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) pillars. It records where the programme contributes, where it creates risk, and what must be evidenced before alignment can be claimed. The mapping uses the figures stated in this summary and has not been independently assessed. Each contribution is a design claim until it has a baseline, a metric and an independent verifier.

SDG contribution map

An audit of the newly incorporated Global Ecosystem Regeneration & Utility Initiative (20-Year Master Plan) confirms that the introduction of the macro-CSR framework fully addresses and bridges the 7 previously excluded UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). By funding this blueprint using a strict 2% corporate pretax profit engine, the Delper Group expands its footprint from isolated industrial hubs into a planet-wide utility network targeting 5.5 million village modules. The sections below show how the 7 previously missing SDGs are explicitly integrated and operationalised within the updated framework.

SDG 1: No Poverty
  • Active Mechanism: The initiative directly introduces 11 million marginalized women into the grassroots economy as equity-holding micro-entrepreneurs running the 31,583 walk-in smart pods.
  • Economic Impact: Injects $23.14 Million USD (Rs. 2,221 Million) in net monthly earnings directly into low-income communities.
SDG 2: Zero Hunger
  • Active Mechanism: Pods provide instant, balanced meals 24/7 via specialized culinary partnerships (Shastry's Kitchen and Shetty's Kitchen).
  • Macro Scale: Connects 5.5 million solar cold-storage nodes to an AI-driven predictive logistics marketplace. This eliminates predatory middleman markups, aims to recover $1.2 Trillion USD in annual post-harvest crop spoilage, and directly targets the structural food deficit.
SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being
  • Active Mechanism: Every rural phase module deploys a telehealth diagnostic room that connects remote villagers to urban specialists.
  • Execution: Integrates over-the-counter wellness shelves inside smart pods and establishes automated telemetry networks to maintain health utility uptimes.
SDG 5: Gender Equality
  • Active Mechanism: The retail micro-commerce engine explicitly mandates a 100% female operator framework for the global urban pod rollout.
  • Execution: Shifts local financial agency to marginalized women by giving them direct ownership stakes in localized digital banking and biometric micro-ATM nodes.
SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation
  • Active Mechanism: Deploys 5-stage RO/UV water ATMs hooked up to 200-litre standalone battery-backed tanks.
  • Macro Scale: Funds deep desilting of community ponds, constructs rainwater harvesting matrices, implements greywater natural reed-bed filtration channels, and deploys water-free composting bio-toilets across 5.5 million villages.
SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities
  • Active Mechanism: Replaces volatile, short-term charity models with a zero-cost infrastructure deployment model for beneficiaries.
  • Execution: Grassroots communities assume zero debt and zero operating obligations. The 2% corporate profit engine distributes asset ownership downward, lowering productivity losses and baseline structural wealth gaps.
SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities
  • Active Mechanism: Stage 1 installs dense, weather-sealed 8 ft by 6 ft by 8.5 ft smart pods inside high-density, low-income urban settlements and transit points.
  • Macro Scale: Ramps into Stage 2 (Years 10–20) to retrofit village arrays into continental smart energy grids, connecting isolated rural zones to national power corridors via bi-directional edge inverters.

Ecosystem verdict

With the integration of the GitHub-hosted Delper-CSR framework, all 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals are now actively addressed through either the primary industrial architecture or the compounding 2% macro-utility fund.

Actions before ESG and SDG claims are relied on

  1. Impact assessment: Commission an independent environmental and social impact assessment for the coastal corridor, nuclear sites and rail routes.
  2. Carbon baseline: Publish a carbon baseline and a net-zero construction pathway that covers cement and steel.
  3. Palm oil policy: Adopt a sourcing policy with certification, traceability and deforestation-free commitments before the palm oil route begins.
  4. Labour and community framework: Set a labour, human-rights and community-engagement framework covering workers across the 560,000 dark factories and affected communities.
  5. Financing evidence: Obtain written confirmation of the IBRD and AIIB guarantee terms, and an independent legal review of the token-based financing.
  6. KPIs and reporting: Define 8 to 12 indicators for the aligned SDGs, each with a baseline, a target and a verifier, and report annually against GRI or ISSB (IFRS S1 and S2).
  7. Group software override policy: Adopt a Group-wide policy that every system making or executing decisions affecting customers, traders, workers, public infrastructure or safety has a designed, tested human override, with a named owner, defined thresholds, and an audit log of each use. Agentic systems also need written limits on their permitted actions, appeal routes for traders, change control for model updates, and a named executive accountable for their decisions. Cover this in the SDG 16 and governance review.

Alignment statements in this section are design-level assessments based on the figures in this summary. They are not an external ESG rating or SDG certification, and they have not been independently verified.

13. Learning Platform: Sana Learn

Sana Learn is proposed as the learning management layer for onboarding, training and compliance across the Delper Group. It combines an LMS and a learning experience platform in one AI-native system. Its role is to deliver and track training. It does not replace the university, engineering or operating systems described elsewhere in this summary.

Features relevant to Delper

  • Course authoring and assessments: course builder, quizzes and tests, and support for instructor-led sessions.
  • Content conversion and import: PDFs can be converted into interactive courses, and existing content can be imported via SCORM.
  • Automated enrollment: programs with enrollment rules, reminders, and certificate generation.
  • HR system integration: automatic enrollment and in-person session scheduling linked to HR records.
  • Virtual classroom: polls, quizzes, reflection threads and breakout rooms for live cohorts.
  • AI tutoring and dashboards: personalized learning paths and performance reporting.
  • Mobile and microlearning: short modules suited to field and factory staff.

Where it fits

Cost and scale

Pricing is not confirmed. Published figures conflict, ranging from $13 per user per year to $13 per user per month, with some listings starting at $8. At $13 per user per year, 1,000 learners cost about $13,000 a year. The 560,000 FDEs would cost about $7.3 million a year, or about $87 million a year at the monthly rate. The Track A and Track B use-of-funds tables have no LMS line, so this cost must be budgeted or negotiated separately.

Recommendation

Run a scoped pilot before any enterprise commitment, such as one partner or supplier cohort or the first FDE group. Obtain written pricing and complete a data-residency review for Indian staff and learners first.

Leadership training for managers

Managers who oversee AI-driven onboarding and sales need training in leading people through change and in setting AI governance controls. We recommend two MIT Sloan Executive Education courses, with enrollment subject to MIT's own admission process:

  • Managing the Human Side of Digital Disruption (primary): A six-week, self-paced online course with live MIT faculty sessions, covering how roles, capabilities and emotions change during digital transition. It can be bought for a whole team.
  • Implementing Agentic AI: Building Your Organizational Playbook (secondary): A short online course, with no technical background needed, that produces a governance framework and a pilot plan. It supports the design of the parameters, escalation rules and human override controls described in Section 14.
  • Designing Organizations for Agentic AI (Harvard Business School Online, complementary): A four-module online course of 20 to 25 hours, with 90 days of access. It covers evaluating and deploying AI agents, redesigning workflows for human-agent collaboration, and applying governance, security and AI sovereignty frameworks. It suits the executives who will oversee the Deloitte-provided CEO function and the agent governance controls in Section 16.

Course details come from MIT Sloan Executive Education and GetSmarter. Training supports the governance controls in this section but does not replace them.

Sana feature and pricing information comes from Sana's published materials and third-party reviews. It has not been verified in a product demonstration, and pricing should be confirmed with the vendor.

14. Global Onboarding

Partners, operators, suppliers and team members joining the Delper Group across regions can start their onboarding once the Group confirms the sign-up route for their market. Onboarding steps are confirmed once the sign-up is complete.

Onboarding terms, eligibility and any regional requirements are set by the Group and the applicable jurisdiction. This link does not constitute an offer of securities or a financing commitment.

Parameter-based automation with human access

Delper's onboarding and sales processes run on defined parameters. Each step follows written rules and thresholds, such as eligibility criteria, document requirements, consent status and approved outreach templates. The system acts only within those parameters. Any case that falls outside them, or that the rules cannot decide, is routed to a person. Every automated process that makes or executes a decision affecting a partner, supplier, operator, team member or prospect has a named human owner, as set out in the Human Override Policy in Section 12.

At any point in onboarding or sales, an applicant, prospect or partner can choose to connect with a human. The request is routed to a named team member, and the person can pause or change the automated steps. Sign-up creates the partner or supplier record in Delper's own systems, and the sign-up route is to be confirmed by the Group.

In sales, AI searches Apollo for prospects that match a Delper service, within Apollo's terms and rate limits. The workflow drafts outreach only for prospects with a lawful basis for contact in their market. A salesperson approves each message before it is sent. Each message identifies Delper and includes an opt-out, and opt-outs are kept in Delper's own CRM and applied across all tools.

Parameters and human override

Each automated process has a named owner, a written set of parameters, a rule for escalating to a person, a control to halt the process, and an audit log of every escalation and override. Applicants and prospects can request a human review of any automated decision that affects them, at any stage.

↑ Index

15. AI Ethics and Governance

Delper uses AI in onboarding, sales prospecting and operations. This section sets out the ethical commitments that apply to those uses. They are proposed commitments, to be approved by the Group before they are relied on.

Principles

  • Human accountability: Every automated process has a named human owner, as set out in Section 12 and the Human Override Policy.
  • Human access: Any applicant, partner, supplier, prospect or team member can ask for a person at any stage, and can request a human review of an automated decision that affects them.
  • Explainable decisions: Each decision to accept, reject, suspend or delay an applicant records the parameters it applied, so the reason can be given in plain language.
  • Consent and lawful basis: Outreach is sent only where a lawful basis exists in the prospect's market, under India's DPDP Act, GDPR and PECR. Each message identifies Delper and offers an opt-out, which is honoured promptly.
  • Data minimisation: Only the data needed for onboarding, compliance and sales is collected, and it is held in Delper's own systems.
  • Fairness: Eligibility and scoring parameters are tested for disparate impact across regions, genders and business sizes before use, and retested at least annually.
  • Transparency about AI: Prospects and applicants are told when they are dealing with an automated process, and when a message was drafted by AI and approved by a person.
  • Safety and security: Automated systems that touch factory operations use the hardware-enforced controls described in the Aegis summary, and are subject to a halt control.

Risks and controls

RiskControl
Wrongful rejection of a partner or supplierHuman review of every rejection, reason recorded, and an appeal route.
Biased parameters excluding groups of applicantsPre-launch and annual fairness testing, with results reported to the Group.
Unlawful or unwanted outreachConsent check before first contact, opt-out list kept in Delper's CRM and applied across all tools.
Workforce displacement in the FDE and hub modelTraining pathways for affected staff, and a documented transition plan before automation is extended.
Misuse of personal data across marketsData residency review for each market, and access limited to named roles.
Unsafe automated action in factoriesHuman approval for any action that changes equipment state, and a tested halt control.

Advanced capability gate

No system with capabilities beyond the approved agent register may be deployed in the Delper business process. This includes general-purpose systems and any system described as artificial general intelligence or superintelligence. Such a system would need a prior ethics review, a documented safety case, an independent safety test, and written approval from GK Bharta. GK Bharta's override, kill switch and sole control of finance and payments apply to any such system in full and cannot be removed or narrowed.

Governance

An AI ethics review is held before any new automated process goes live, and each automated process is reviewed at least annually. The review records the parameters, owners, escalation rules and fairness results. Reports go to the Group board. Leadership training in AI governance, set out in Section 13, supports these reviews.

Points to confirm

EY: GK Bharta can stop or replace the engagement, but it cannot alter the audit conclusions. This keeps the audit independent.

Named owners: Section 12 gives each automated process a named Delper owner with a halt control. If the kill switch sits only with GK Bharta, that halt control must be reconciled with Section 12.

Hardware safety: Equipment-level controls in the Aegis platform, such as the physical write-lock, stay in force and are not affected by the kill switch.

Cryptography and QKD pilot

Post-quantum cryptography is the baseline for the whole business process. It covers the ledger, APIs, partner links, the Aegis firmware signing and the data stores, and runs on existing networks and devices. NIST published its first post-quantum standards in 2024 (FIPS 203 for key exchange, FIPS 204 and 205 for signatures).

QKD is not applied across the whole process. It is limited to a pilot between the four hubs (Dubai, Singapore, Bengaluru/Mumbai and London), to be started only after the platform is live and proven. Scenario A of the pilot is estimated at USD 1.0M to 4.4M one-off and USD 0.1M to 0.3M a year in maintenance, before any tariff impact. Extension to a critical network of about 50 links (USD 16M to 90M) is subject to the pilot results and Group approval. Whole-process QKD, covering about 80,000 factory links, is not feasible at an estimated USD 16 billion or more in hardware.

Security assurance statement

The Delper global business process is designed to be resilient and recoverable. It is not represented as hacker-free. QKD protects key exchange on the links it runs over, and detects eavesdropping on those links. It does not protect endpoints, software, trusted relay nodes, availability or people. Security therefore rests on the layered controls below, not on QKD alone.

Control layerControl in this planReference

The target is containment in under 3 seconds. On factory equipment, a sealed quarantine store that host software cannot clear, and signed patches applied at every step.Aegis summary, Section 20; Section 16 kill switch

Financial controlsPayments operated by GK Bharta finance with a 2-day lead time; EY reviews controls for the financial sideSection 16, finance and payments

Self-quarantine: Automated quarantine is the containment layer. It acts within seconds to isolate a threat, and the GK Bharta kill switch remains the final halt. The Aegis summary sets the 3-second containment target and cites CrowdStrike figures, including an average eCrime breakout of about 29 minutes. These figures are as quoted in the Aegis summary and need confirming against primary sources. The Aegis summary also excludes its self-quarantine segment from several of its own financial sections, so it isn't used to size the investment here.

The aim is detection, containment and recovery without loss of money or control. No control set can guarantee that no attack succeeds.

Payment acceptance processor (Adyen, option)

Adyen is a global payments platform that accepts card, wallet and local payments and operates in India under Reserve Bank of India authorisations. The plan names Stripe, Adyen and Worldpay as payment rails for the POS layer. The table maps Adyen's published claims to Delper. These are the company's own claims and have not been verified.

Finance rule: Adyen would handle incoming customer payments only. It would hold no authority over outgoing payments. GK Bharta alone operates finance and makes all outgoing payments, with a 2-day lead time, and this is unchanged. Any settlement from Adyen to Delper should pass through GK Bharta finance. Adopting Adyen would need approval, a contract that gives GK Bharta the kill switch over its services, and a place in the responsibility matrix. Its price is not stated on the page.

Product master data (PiLog Article Master, option)

PiLog Article Master is a retail product-data platform. It uses AI matching to flag duplicate product records, applies governance workflows before records reach SAP Retail, and builds one golden article record per product. Its use case is retail, so it fits the supplier and merchandise data in the supply-chain and channel work rather than the token or service flows. The table maps its claims to Delper. These are the vendor's own claims and have not been verified.

Limits: The matching engine only recommends. Final approval stays with a human steward, consistent with Section 12. Adopting it would add a new provider, so it would need approval, a contract that gives GK Bharta the kill switch over its work, and a place in the responsibility matrix. Its price is not stated.

Vendor claimDelper useCheck before adoption

No agent goes live in a market until that market's compliance conditions are signed off. The gate applies to each agent in each market, and the earliest go-live month shown below is a floor, not a start date. The licence programme (VARA, MAS, FCA, DFSA, FinCEN, NY BitLicense and MiCA) sets the market-by-market timing. Sign-off sits with the named owner, and GK Bharta can halt any agent at any time through the kill switch.
